Berbers.fact: Though nominally serving at the caliph's pleasure, Al Aghlab and his successors, the Aghlabids, ruled independently until 909, presiding over a court that became a center of learning and culture. Just to the west of Aghlabid lands, Abd ar Rahman ibn Rustam ruled most of the central Maghreb from Tahert, south-west of Algiers.

Berbers.subject: Indian Languages
Berbers.question: The rulers of the _____ imamate (761–909), each an Ibadi imam, were elected by leading citizens
Berbers.fact: The rulers of the Rustamid imamate (761–909), each an Ibadi imam, were elected by leading citizens. The Rustamid imams failed, by choice or by neglect, to organize a reliable standing army.

Berbers.subject: Indian Languages
Berbers.question: The court at _____ was noted for its support of scholarship in mathematics, astronomy, astrology, theology, and law
Berbers.fact: Just to the west of Aghlabid lands, Abd ar Rahman ibn Rustam ruled most of the central Maghreb from Tahert, south-west of Algiers. The court at Tahert was noted for its support of scholarship in mathematics, astronomy, astrology, theology, and law.

Berbers.fact: This important factor, accompanied by the dynasty's eventual collapse into decadence, opened the way for Tahert's demise under the assault of the Fatimids. Berbers.fact: It was chosen as the capital because of its proximity to the sea, and the promontory on which an important military settlement had been since the time of the Phoenicians.

Berbers.fact: The biographical dictionary of Ibn Khallikan preserves the record of the Berber predominance in the invasion of 711, in the entry on Tariq ibn Ziyad.

Berbers.subject: Indian Languages

Berbers.fact: A second mixed army of Arabs and Berbers came in 712 under Ibn Nusayr himself.

Berbers.fact: They supposedly helped the Umayyad caliph Abd ar-Rahman I in al-Andalus, because his mother was a Berber.

Berbers.fact: It was at this time that the positions of Arabs and Berbers were regularized across the Iberian peninsula. Berbers were positioned in many of the most mountainous regions of Spain, such as Granada, the Pyrenees, Cantabria, and Galicia.

Berbers.fact: When Pelagius revolted in Asturias, it was against a Berber governor. The expulsion of the Berber garrisons from central Asturias, following the battle of Covadonga, contributed to the eventual formation of the independent Asturian kingdom.

Berbers.subject: Indian Languages

Berbers.fact: By the late 710s, there was a Berber governor in Leon or Gijon. When Pelagius revolted in Asturias, it was against a Berber governor.

Berbers.subject: Indian Languages

Berbers.fact: Many Berbers were settled in what were then the frontier lands near Toledo, Talavera, and Mérida, Mérida becoming a major Berber stronghold in the eighth century. The Berber garrison in Talavera would later be commanded by Amrus ibn Yusuf and was involved in military operations against rebels in Toledo in the late 700s and early 800s.

Berbers.subject: Indian Languages
Berbers.question: They were not settled in the major cities of the south, and were generally kept in the frontier zones away from _____
Berbers.fact: They were not settled in the major cities of the south, and were generally kept in the frontier zones away from Cordoba.

Berbers.subject: Indian Languages

Berbers.fact: Roger Collins cites the work of Pierre Guichard to argue that Berber groups in Iberia retained their own distinctive social organization.

Berbers.subject: Indian Languages

Berbers.fact: According to this traditional view of Arab and Berber culture in the Iberian peninsula, Berber society was highly impermeable to outside influences, whereas Arabs became assimilated and Hispanized.

Berbers.subject: Indian Languages

Berbers.fact: In 731, the eastern Pyrenees were under the control of Berber forces garrisoned in the major towns under the command of Munuza.

Berbers.fact: However, governor Abd ar-Rahman attacked Munuza before he was ready, and, besieging him, defeated him at Cerdanya. Because of the alliance with Munnuza, Abd ar-Rahman wanted to punish Eudo, and his punitive expedition ended in the Arab defeat at Poitiers.

Berbers.subject: Indian Languages
Berbers.question: Because of the alliance with _____, Abd ar-Rahman wanted to punish Eudo, and his punitive expedition ended in the Arab defeat at Poitiers
Berbers.fact: Munnuza attempted a Berber uprising against the Arabs in Spain, citing mistreatment of Berbers by Arabic judges in north Africa, and made an alliance with Duke Eudo of Aquitaine. Berbers.fact: Medieval Egyptian historian Al-Hakam wrote that there was a major Berber revolt in north Africa in 740–741, led by Masayra.

Berbers.subject: Indian Languages
Berbers.question: Initially, these attacks were unsuccessful; but eventually _____ destroyed the rebels, secured all the crossing points to Spain, and then returned to his governorship

Berbers.subject: Indian Languages
Berbers.question: Although Masayra was killed by his own followers, the revolt spread and the _____ rebels defeated three Arab armies
Berbers.fact: After Charles Martel attacked Arab ally Maurontus at Marseille in 739, governor Uqba planned a punitive attack against the Franks, but news of a Berber revolt in north Africa made him turn back when he reached Zaragoza. Instead, according to the Chronicle of 754, Uqba carried out an attack against Berber fortresses in Africa.

Berbers.subject: Indian Languages

Berbers.fact: After the defeat of the third army, which included elite units of Syrians commanded by Kulthum and Balj, the Berber revolt spread further.

Berbers.subject: Indian Languages
Berbers.question: At this time, the _____ military colonies in Spain revolted
Berbers.fact: Although Masayra was killed by his own followers, the revolt spread and the Berber rebels defeated three Arab armies. After the defeat of the third army, which included elite units of Syrians commanded by Kulthum and Balj, the Berber revolt spread further.

Berbers.subject: Indian Languages

Berbers.fact: At the same time, Uqba died and was replaced by Ibn Qatan. Ibn Qatan invited Balj and his Syrian troops, who were at that time in Ceuta, to cross to the Iberian peninsula to fight against the Berbers.

Berbers.fact: Roger Collins argues that the Great Berber revolt facilitated the establishment of the Kingdom of Asturias and altered the demographics of the Berber population in the Iberian peninsula, specifically contributing to the Berber departure from the northwest of the peninsula. When the Arabs first invaded the peninsula, Berber groups were in the northwest.

Berbers.subject: Indian Languages

Berbers.fact: Some presence of Berbers in the northwest may have been maintained at first, but after the 740s there is no more mention of the northwestern Berbers in the sources.

Berbers.subject: Indian Languages

Berbers.fact: As the governor Ibn Habib was seeking him, he then fled to the more powerful Zenata Berber confederacy, who were enemies of Ibn Habib.

Berbers.subject: Indian Languages

Berbers.fact: Since the Zenata had been part of the initial invasion force of al-Andalus, and were still present in the Iberian peninsula, this gave Abd ar-Rahman a base of support in al-Andalus, although he seems to have drawn most of his support from portions of Balj's army that were still loyal to the Umayyads. Abd ar-Rahman crossed to Spain in 756 and declared himself the legitimate Umayyad ruler of al-Andalus.

Berbers.subject: Indian Languages

Berbers.subject: Indian Languages

Berbers.fact: After losing the initial battle near Cordoba, Yusuf fled to Mérida, where he raised a large Berber army, with which he marched on Seville, but was defeated by forces loyal to Abd ar-Rahman.

Berbers.subject: Indian Languages
Berbers.question: Yusuf's cousin _____ ibn Urwa continued to resist Abd ar-Rahman from Toledo until 764, and the sons of Yusuf revolted again in 785
Berbers.fact: Yusuf's cousin Hisham ibn Urwa continued to resist Abd ar-Rahman from Toledo until 764, and the sons of Yusuf revolted again in 785.

Berbers.fact: As emir of al-Andalus, Abd ar-Rahman I faced persistent opposition from Berber groups, including the Zenata. Andalusi Berber Salih ibn Tarif declared himself a prophet and ruled the Bargawata Berber confederation in Morocco in the 770s.

Berbers.fact: Andalusi Berber Salih ibn Tarif declared himself a prophet and ruled the Bargawata Berber confederation in Morocco in the 770s.

Berbers.fact: In 768, a Miknasa Berber named Shaqya ibn Abd al-Walid declared himself a Fatimid imam, claiming descent from Fatimah and Ali.

Berbers.fact: Shaqya first killed the Umayyad governor of the fortress of Santaver (near Roman Ercavica), and subsequently ravaged the district surrounding Coria. In 772, Shaqya defeated an Umayyad force by a ruse and killed the governor of the fortress of Medellin.

Berbers.fact: Abd ar-Rahman sent out armies to fight him in 769, 770, and 771; but Shaqya avoided them by moving into the mountains. In 775, a Berber garrison in Coria declared allegiance to Shaqya, but Abd ar-Rahman retook the town and chased the Berbers into the mountains.

Berbers.fact: He also compares these leaders to pre-Islamic leaders Dihya and Kusaila.

Berbers.fact: The Toledo rebellion was sufficiently weakened that Amrus was able to enter Toledo and convince its inhabitants to submit.

Berbers.fact: Collins argues that unassimilated Berber garrisons in al-Andalus engaged in local vendettas and feuds, such as the conflict with the Banu Mahsa.

Berbers.fact: Tarragona was uninhabited for seven years until the Frankish conquest of Barcelona led to its reoccupation.

Berbers.fact: Ibn Hafsun rebelled in 880, was captured, then escaped in 883 to his base in Bobastro.

After taking the city of Kairouan and overthrowing the Aghlabids in 909, the Mahdi Ubayd Allah was installed by the Kutama as Imam and Caliph, which posed a direct challenge to the Umayyad's own claim.

Berbers.fact: The Fatimids gained overlordship over the Idrisids, then launched a conquest of the Maghreb.

Berbers.subject: Indian Languages
Berbers.question: Rather than fighting each other directly, the _____ and Umayyads competed for Berber allegiances
Berbers.fact: The Fatimids gained overlordship over the Idrisids, then launched a conquest of the Maghreb. Rather than fighting each other directly, the Fatimids and Umayyads competed for Berber allegiances.

Berbers.subject: Indian Languages

Berbers.fact: In turn, this would contribute to the establishment of the Almoravid dynasty and Almohad Caliphate, which would have a major impact on al-Andalus and contribute to the end of the Umayyad caliphate.

Berbers.fact: With the help of his new mercenary forces, Abd ar-Rahman launched a series of attacks on parts of the Iberian peninsula that had fallen away from Umayyad allegiance.

Berbers.subject: Indian Languages

Berbers.fact: In the 920s he campaigned against the areas that rebelled under Umar ibn Hafsun and refused to submit until the 920s.

Berbers.subject: Indian Languages
Berbers.question: He conquered Mérida in 928–929, Ceuta in 931, and _____ in 932
Berbers.fact: He conquered Mérida in 928–929, Ceuta in 931, and Toledo in 932.

Berbers.subject: Indian Languages

Berbers.fact: In 934 he began a campaign in the north against Ramiro II of Leon and Muhammad ibn Hashim al-Tujibi, the governor of Zaragoza.

Berbers.subject: Indian Languages
Berbers.question: From 935 to 937, he confronted the _____, defeating them in 937
Berbers.fact: From 935 to 937, he confronted the Tujibids, defeating them in 937.

Berbers.subject: Indian Languages
Berbers.question: In 939, _____ II defeated the combined Umayyad and Tujibid armies in the Battle of Simancas

According to Ibn Hayyan, after inconclusively confronting al-Tujibi on the Ebro, Abd ar-Rahman briefly forced the Kingdom of Pamplona into submission, ravaged Castile and Alava, and met Ramiro II in an inconclusive battle.

Berbers.subject: Indian Languages
Berbers.question: Umayyad influence in western _____ spread through diplomacy rather than conquest
Berbers.fact: Umayyad influence in western North Africa spread through diplomacy rather than conquest.

Berbers.subject: Indian Languages
Berbers.question: The Umayyads sought out alliances with various _____ confederacies
Berbers.fact: The Umayyads sought out alliances with various Berber confederacies.

Berbers.subject: Indian Languages
Berbers.question: These would declare loyalty to the _____ caliphate in opposition to the Fatimids
Berbers.fact: In 939, Ramiro II defeated the combined Umayyad and Tujibid armies in the Battle of Simancas. Umayyad influence in western North Africa spread through diplomacy rather than conquest.

Berbers.subject: Indian Languages
Berbers.question: During this time, mints in cities on the _____ coast—Fes, Sijilmasa, Sfax, and al-Nakur—occasionally issued coins with the names of Umayyad caliphs, showing the extent of Umayyad diplomatic influence
Berbers.fact: During this time, mints in cities on the Moroccan coast—Fes, Sijilmasa, Sfax, and al-Nakur—occasionally issued coins with the names of Umayyad caliphs, showing the extent of Umayyad diplomatic influence.

Berbers.subject: Indian Languages
Berbers.question: The text of a letter of friendship from a Berber leader to the _____ caliph has been preserved in the work of 'Isa al-Razi
Berbers.fact: These would declare loyalty to the Umayyad caliphate in opposition to the Fatimids. The Umayyads would send gifts, including embroidered silk ceremonial cloaks.

Berbers.subject: Indian Languages
Berbers.question: Following Abd ar-_____'s proclamation of the new Umayyad caliphate in Cordoba, the Umayyads placed a great emphasis on the Umayyad membership of the Quraysh tribe
Berbers.fact: During Abd ar-Rahman's reign, tensions increased between the three distinct components of the Muslim community in al-Andalus: Berbers, Saqaliba (European slaves), and those of Arab or mixed Arab and Gothic descent. Following Abd ar-Rahman's proclamation of the new Umayyad caliphate in Cordoba, the Umayyads placed a great emphasis on the Umayyad membership of the Quraysh tribe.

Berbers.subject: Indian Languages
Berbers.question: This led to a fashion, in _____, for claiming pure Arab ancestry as opposed to descent from freed slaves
Berbers.fact: Following Abd ar-Rahman's proclamation of the new Umayyad caliphate in Cordoba, the Umayyads placed a great emphasis on the Umayyad membership of the Quraysh tribe. This led to a fashion, in Cordoba, for claiming pure Arab ancestry as opposed to descent from freed slaves.

Berbers.subject: Indian Languages

Berbers.fact: Claims of descent from Visigothic noble families also became common.

Berbers.subject: Indian Languages

Berbers.fact: The Zirids in turn divided their territories, assigning some to the Hammadid branch of the family to govern. The Hammadids became independent in 1014, with their capital at Qal'at Beni-Hammad.

Berbers.subject: Indian Languages
Berbers.question: The Hammadids became independent in _____, with their capital at Qal'at Beni-Hammad
Berbers.fact: The Hammadids became independent in 1014, with their capital at Qal'at Beni-Hammad.

Berbers.subject: Indian Languages
Berbers.question: With the withdrawal of the _____ to Egypt, however, the rivalry with the Umayyads decreased
Berbers.fact: When the Fatimids moved their capital to Egypt in 969, they left north Africa in charge of viceroys from the Zirid clan of Sanhaja Berbers, who were Fatimid loyalists and enemies of the Zenata. Berbers.subject: Indian Languages

Berbers.fact: Al-Hakam II sent Muhammad Ibn Abī 'Āmir to north Africa in 973–974 to act as qadi al qudat (chief justice) to the Berber groups that had accepted Umayyad authority.

Berbers.subject: Indian Languages

Berbers.fact: In 1009, Sanchuelo had himself proclaimed Hisham II's successor, and then went on military campaign.

Berbers.question: As he marched back to _____ his own Berber mercenaries abandoned him
Berbers.fact: As he marched back to Cordoba his own Berber mercenaries abandoned him. Knowing the strength of ill feeling against them in Cordoba, they thought Sanchuelo would be unable to protect them, and so they went elsewhere in order to survive and secure their own interests.

Berbers.subject: Indian Languages
Berbers.question: Knowing the strength of ill feeling against them in _____, they thought Sanchuelo would be unable to protect them, and so they went elsewhere in order to survive and secure their own interests
Berbers.fact: As he marched back to Cordoba his own Berber mercenaries abandoned him. Knowing the strength of ill feeling against them in Cordoba, they thought Sanchuelo would be unable to protect them, and so they went elsewhere in order to survive and secure their own interests.

Berbers.subject: Indian Languages
Berbers.question: Sanchuelo was left with only a few followers, and was captured and killed in _____
Berbers.fact: Sanchuelo was left with only a few followers, and was captured and killed in 1009.

Berbers.subject: Indian Languages
Berbers.question: Hisham II abdicated and was succeeded by _____ al-Mahdi
Berbers.fact: Hisham II abdicated and was succeeded by Muhammad II al-Mahdi. Marching on Cordoba, they defeated Saqaliba general Wadih and forced Muhammad II al-Mahdi to flee to Toledo.

Berbers.subject: Indian Languages
Berbers.question: They obtained logistical support from _____ of Castile
Berbers.fact: They obtained logistical support from Count Sancho Garcia of Castile.

Berbers.subject: Indian Languages
Berbers.question: Marching on _____, they defeated Saqaliba general Wadih and forced Muhammad II al-Mahdi to flee to Toledo
Berbers.fact: Marching on Cordoba, they defeated Saqaliba general Wadih and forced Muhammad II al-Mahdi to flee to Toledo. Wadih and al-Mahdi formed an alliance with the Counts of Barcelona and Urgell and marched back on Cordoba.

Berbers.subject: Indian Languages
Berbers.question: They then installed _____ as caliph, and based themselves in the Madinat al-Zahra to avoid friction with the local population
Berbers.fact: Having abandoned Sanchuelo, the Berbers who had formed his army turned to support another ambitious Umayyad, Sulayman. They then installed Sulayman as caliph, and based themselves in the Madinat al-Zahra to avoid friction with the local population.

Berbers.subject: Indian Languages
Berbers.question: Wadih and al-Mahdi formed an alliance with the Counts of _____ and Urgell and marched back on Cordoba
Berbers.fact: Wadih and al-Mahdi formed an alliance with the Counts of Barcelona and Urgell and marched back on Cordoba.

Berbers.subject: Indian Languages
Berbers.question: They defeated Sulayman and the Berber forces in a battle near Cordoba in _____
Berbers.fact: They defeated Sulayman and the Berber forces in a battle near Cordoba in 1010.

Berbers.subject: Indian Languages
Berbers.question: However, he was defeated in battle near _____
Berbers.fact: However, he was defeated in battle near Marbella.

Berbers.subject: Indian Languages
Berbers.question: They methodically destroyed _____'s suburbs, pinning the inhabitants inside the old Roman walls and destroying the Madinat al-Zahra
Berbers.fact: The Berbers turned around and besieged Cordoba. They methodically destroyed Cordoba's suburbs, pinning the inhabitants inside the old Roman walls and destroying the Madinat al-Zahra.

Berbers.subject: Indian Languages
Berbers.question: Wadih's allies killed him, and the _____ garrison surrendered with the expectation of amnesty
Berbers.fact: They methodically destroyed Cordoba's suburbs, pinning the inhabitants inside the old Roman walls and destroying the Madinat al-Zahra. Wadih's allies killed him, and the Cordoba garrison surrendered with the expectation of amnesty.

Berbers.subject: Indian Languages

Berbers.fact: Ibn Idhari said that the installation of Sulayman in 1013 was the moment when "the rule of the Berbers began in Cordoba and that of the Umayyads ended, after it had existed for two hundred and sixty eight years and forty-three days". After the fall of Cordoba in 1013, the Saqaliba fled from the city to secure their own fiefdoms.

Berbers.subject: Indian Languages
Berbers.question: After the fall of Cordoba in _____, the Saqaliba fled from the city to secure their own fiefdoms
Berbers.fact: Ibn Idhari said that the installation of Sulayman in 1013 was the moment when "the rule of the Berbers began in Cordoba and that of the Umayyads ended, after it had existed for two hundred and sixty eight years and forty-three days". After the fall of Cordoba in 1013, the Saqaliba fled from the city to secure their own fiefdoms.

Berbers.subject: Indian Languages

Berbers.fact: The Taifa period ended when a Berber dynasty—the Moroccan Almoravids—took over al-Andalus; they were succeeded by the Almohad dynasty of Morocco, during which time al-Andalus flourished.

Berbers.subject: Indian Languages
Berbers.question: One group of _____ seized Orihuela from its Berber garrison and took control of the entire region
Berbers.fact: After the fall of Cordoba in 1013, the Saqaliba fled from the city to secure their own fiefdoms. One group of Saqaliba seized Orihuela from its Berber garrison and took control of the entire region.

Berbers.subject: Indian Languages
Berbers.question: After the fall of Cordoba, the Zirids took over Granada in _____, forming the Zirid kingdom of Granada
Berbers.fact: After the fall of Cordoba in 1013, the Saqaliba fled from the city to secure their own fiefdoms. After the fall of Cordoba, the Zirids took over Granada in 1013, forming the Zirid kingdom of Granada.

Berbers.subject: Indian Languages
Berbers.question: The Saqaliba Khayran, with his own Umayyad figurehead Abd ar-Rahman IV al-Murtada, attempted to seize Granada from the Zirids in _____, but failed
Berbers.fact: The Saqaliba Khayran, with his own Umayyad figurehead Abd ar-Rahman IV al-Murtada, attempted to seize Granada from the Zirids in 1018, but failed.

Berbers.subject: Indian Languages
Berbers.question: Khayran then executed Abd ar-_____ IV
Berbers.fact: The Saqaliba Khayran, with his own Umayyad figurehead Abd ar-Rahman IV al-Murtada, attempted to seize Granada from the Zirids in 1018, but failed. Khayran then executed Abd ar-Rahman IV.

Berbers.subject: Indian Languages
Berbers.question: Khayran's son, Zuhayr, also made war on the Zirid kingdom of Granada, but was killed in _____
Berbers.fact: Khayran's son, Zuhayr, also made war on the Zirid kingdom of Granada, but was killed in 1038.

Berbers.subject: Indian Languages
Berbers.question: In Cordoba, conflicts continued between the _____ rulers and those of the citizenry who saw themselves as Arab
Berbers.fact: In Cordoba, conflicts continued between the Berber rulers and those of the citizenry who saw themselves as Arab. After being installed as caliph with Berber support, Sulayman was pressured into distributing southern provinces to his Berber allies.

Berbers.subject: Indian Languages
Berbers.question: After being installed as caliph with Berber support, _____ was pressured into distributing southern provinces to his Berber allies
Berbers.fact: After being installed as caliph with Berber support, Sulayman was pressured into distributing southern provinces to his Berber allies.

Berbers.subject: Indian Languages

Berbers.fact: In Cordoba, conflicts continued between the Berber rulers and those of the citizenry who saw themselves as Arab. The Sanhaja departed from Cordoba at this time.

Berbers.fact: The Zenata Berber Hammudids received the important districts of Ceuta and Algeciras.

Berbers.subject: Indian Languages

Berbers.fact: The Hammudids claimed a family relation to the Idrisids, and thus traced their ancestry to the caliph Ali.

Berbers.subject: Indian Languages
Berbers.question: In _____ they rebelled in Ceuta, claiming to be supporting the restoration of Hisham II
Berbers.fact: In 1016 they rebelled in Ceuta, claiming to be supporting the restoration of Hisham II.

Berbers.subject: Indian Languages
Berbers.question: They took control of Málaga, then marched on _____, taking it and executing Sulayman and his family
Berbers.fact: They took control of Málaga, then marched on Cordoba, taking it and executing Sulayman and his family.

Berbers.subject: Indian Languages

Berbers.fact: The Hammudids claimed a family relation to the Idrisids, and thus traced their ancestry to the caliph Ali. Ali ibn Hammud al-Nasir declared himself caliph, a position he held for two years.

Berbers.fact: The last Hammudid caliph reigned until 1027.

Berbers.subject: Indian Languages

Berbers.fact: The Hammudids were then expelled from Cordoba, where there was still a great deal of anti-Berber sentiment.

Berbers.subject: Indian Languages

Berbers.fact: The Hammudids remained in Málaga until expelled by the Zirids in 1056.

Berbers.subject: Indian Languages

Berbers.fact: The Zirids of Granada controlled Málaga until 1073, after which separate Zirid kings retained control over the taifas of Granada and Malaga until the Almoravid conquest.

Berbers.subject: Indian Languages
Berbers.question: During the taifa period, the _____ dynasty, based in Badajoz, controlled a large territory centered on the Guadiana River valley
Berbers.fact: During the taifa period, the Aftasid dynasty, based in Badajoz, controlled a large territory centered on the Guadiana River valley. The area of Aftasid control was very large, stretching from the Sierra Morena and the taifas of Mértola and Silves in the south, to the Campo de Calatrava in the west, the Montes de Toledo in the northwest, and nearly as far as Oporto in the northeast.

Berbers.subject: Indian Languages
Berbers.question: According to _____, during the taifa period genealogy continued to be an obsession of the upper classes in al-Andalus
Berbers.fact: According to Bernard Reilly, during the taifa period genealogy continued to be an obsession of the upper classes in al-Andalus.

Berbers.subject: Indian Languages

Berbers.fact: Most wanted to trace their lineage back to the Syrian and Yemeni Arabs who accompanied the invasion.

Berbers.subject: Indian Languages
Berbers.question: Reilly further argues that "distinctions between Arab, _____, and slave were not the stuff of serious politics, either within or between the taifas
Berbers.fact: In contrast, tracing descent from the Berbers who came with the same invasion "was to be stigmatized as of inferior birth". Reilly further argues that "distinctions between Arab, Berber, and slave were not the stuff of serious politics, either within or between the taifas.

Berbers.subject: Indian Languages
Berbers.question: Ethnic rivalry was one of the most important factors driving _____ politics
Berbers.fact: It was the individual family that was the unit of political activity." Ethnic rivalry was one of the most important factors driving Andalusi politics.

Berbers.fact: Berbers made up as much as 20% of the population of the occupied territory.

Berbers.fact: In the mid-11th century, they allied with the Guddala and Massufa Berber.

Berbers.fact: At that time, the Almoravid leader Yahya ibn Ibrahim went on a hajj.

Berbers.fact: On his way back he met Malikite preachers in Kairouan, and invited them to his land. Malikite disciple Abd Allah ibn Yasin accepted the invitation.

Berbers.subject: Indian Languages
Berbers.question: Malikite disciple _____ ibn Yasin accepted the invitation
Berbers.fact: Malikite disciple Abd Allah ibn Yasin accepted the invitation.

Berbers.subject: Indian Languages
Berbers.question: Traveling to _____, he established a military monastery or ribat where he trained a highly motivated and disciplined fighting force
Berbers.fact: Traveling to Morocco, he set up a military monastery or ribat where he trained a highly motivated and disciplined fighting force.

Berbers.subject: Indian Languages
Berbers.question: In _____ and 1055, employing these specially trained forces, Almoravid leader Yahya ibn Umar defeated the Kingdom of Ghana and the Zenata Berber
Berbers.fact: In 1054 and 1055, employing these specially trained forces, Almoravid leader Yahya ibn Umar defeated the Kingdom of Ghana and the Zenata Berber.

Berbers.subject: Indian Languages

Berbers.fact: Forced to resolve a Sanhaja civil war, he left control of the Moroccan conquests to his brother, Yusuf ibn Tashfin.

Berbers.subject: Indian Languages
Berbers.question: Yusuf continued to conquer territory; and following Abu Bakr's death in _____, he became the Almoravid leader
Berbers.fact: Yusuf continued to conquer territory; and following Abu Bakr's death in 1087, he became the Almoravid leader.

Berbers.subject: Indian Languages

Berbers.fact: After their loss of Cordoba, the Hammudids had occupied Algeciras and Ceuta.

Berbers.subject: Indian Languages

Berbers.fact: After their loss of Cordoba, the Hammudids had occupied Algeciras and Ceuta. In the mid-11th century, the Hammudids lost control of their Iberian possessions, but retained a small taifa kingdom based in Ceuta.

Berbers.subject: Indian Languages

Berbers.fact: In 1083, Yusuf ibn Tashufin conquered Ceuta.

Berbers.subject: Indian Languages

Berbers.fact: In the same year, al-Mutamid, king of the Taifa of Seville, traveled to Morocco to appeal to Yusuf for help against King Alfonso VI of Castile. After the fall of Toledo to Alfonso VI in 1085, al-Mutamid appealed again to Yusuf.

Berbers.subject: Indian Languages
Berbers.question: Earlier, in _____, the king of Badajoz, al-Mutawakkil, had appealed to Yusuf for help against Alfonso
Berbers.fact: Earlier, in 1079, the king of Badajoz, al-Mutawakkil, had appealed to Yusuf for help against Alfonso.

Berbers.subject: Indian Languages

Berbers.fact: After the fall of Toledo to Alfonso VI in 1085, al-Mutamid appealed again to Yusuf.

Berbers.fact: This time, financed by the taifa kings of Iberia, Yusuf crossed to al-Andalus and took direct personal control of Algeciras in 1086.

Berbers.fact: They lived primarily in three states or confederations: the Kingdom of Ait Abbas, Kingdom of Kuku, and the principality of Aït Jubar. Berbers.fact: They lived primarily in three states or confederations: the Kingdom of Ait Abbas, Kingdom of Kuku, and the principality of Aït Jubar. Berbers.fact: It is referred to in the Spanish historiography as reino de Labes; sometimes more commonly referred to by its ruling family, the Mokrani, in Berber At Muqran (Arabic: أولاد مقران Ouled Moqrane).

Berbers.subject: Indian Languages

Berbers.fact: The most serious native revolt against colonial power in French Algeria since the time of Abd al-Qadir broke out in 1871 in the Kabylie and spread through much of Algeria. By April 1871, 250 tribes had risen, or nearly a third of Algeria's population.

Berbers.fact: In the aftermath of this revolt and until 1892, the Kabyle myth, which supposed a variety of stereotypes based on a binary between Arabs and Kabyle people, reached its climax.

Berbers.subject: Indian Languages
Berbers.question: In _____, Morocco was divided into French and Spanish zones
Berbers.fact: In 1912, Morocco was divided into French and Spanish zones.

Berbers.fact: In July 1921, the Spanish army in northeastern Morocco, under Manuel Silvestre, were routed by the forces of Abd el-Krim, in what became known in Spain as the Disaster of Annual.

Berbers.subject: Indian Languages

Berbers.fact: In July 1921, the Spanish army in northeastern Morocco, under Manuel Silvestre, were routed by the forces of Abd el-Krim, in what became known in Spain as the Disaster of Annual. The Spaniards may have lost up to 22,000 soldiers at Annual and in subsequent fighting.

Cosmogony.subject: Indian Languages
Cosmogony.question: The _____ was Theory or model concerning the origin of the universe.
Cosmogony.fact: Cosmogony, also spelled as cosmogeny, or cosmogenesis, is any model concerning the origin of the cosmos or the universe. Ancient Greece developed a cosmogony focused on the origin of matter, space, and time with a transition from Chaos to Cosmos.

Cosmogony.subject: Indian Languages
Cosmogony.question: The standard cosmological model of the early development of the universe is the _____ theory, but it is based on a model known to fail at the very earliest times
Cosmogony.fact: The standard cosmological model of the early development of the universe is the Big Bang theory, but it is based on a model known to fail at the very earliest times.

Cosmogony.subject: Indian Languages

Cosmogony.fact: First, the observable universe is much more homogeneous than an extrapolated Big Bang can account for.

Cosmogony.subject: Indian Languages
Cosmogony.question: While inflation has been successful in developing an initial state for _____ models, it does not by itself describe the origin of the universe
Cosmogony.fact: When combined with the Big Bang and other concepts of cosmology, inflation becomes the consensus or standard model of cosmology, a model which successfully predicts details of large scale structure and the CMB. While inflation has been successful in developing an initial state for Big Bang models, it does not by itself describe the origin of the universe.
